export_probe.name: accumulated_deuterated_methane_prefill_count
export_probe.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative amount of deuterated methane introduced during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory. It represents neutral CD4 molecules before plasma breakdown, not the post-breakdown gas-injection inventory.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm prefill} = \int_{t_0}^{t_b} \dot{N}_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm CD_4}(t)\,dt = 10N_{\rm CD_4}^{\rm prefill}
$$

where $N_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm prefill}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron inventory, $\dot{N}_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm CD_4}$ is the [deuterated methane source rate](name:deuterated_methane_source_rate), $t_0$ and $t_b$ delimit prefill before breakdown, and $N_{\rm CD_4}^{\rm prefill}$ is the accumulated number of CD4 molecules. The factor ten is the total electron count of one fully ionizable CD4 molecule. The species-resolved quantity contributes to the [accumulated total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count), which sums equivalent-electron inventories across gas species.

rows.name: parallel_plasma_velocity
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
The parallel plasma velocity is the projection of the bulk [plasma velocity](name:plasma_velocity) onto the local magnetic-field direction. It represents the mass-weighted flow of all contributing plasma species along magnetic field lines.

The parallel component is defined by:

$$
v_\parallel = \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{cm} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}, \qquad \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{cm}$ is the center-of-mass plasma velocity, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the corresponding unit vector. Unlike the [radial plasma velocity](name:radial_plasma_velocity), this quantity follows the local magnetic-field direction rather than the outward major-radius direction.

The quantity is a bulk-plasma projection, not a species-resolved flow or a diamagnetic-drift velocity.

rows.name: krypton_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
The krypton source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral krypton with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Each neutral krypton atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ equivalent electrons to the equivalent particle inventory; this accounting uses nuclear charge and does not imply ionization at the injection location.

The defining relation for krypton injection is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton equivalent-electron source rate in equivalent-electron counts per second, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the neutral krypton atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is the atomic number of krypton.

This is the krypton-species contribution to [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) and is the instantaneous time derivative of [accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) when the same equivalent-electron accounting is used. It excludes krypton supplied by mechanisms other than gas injection and differs from gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection, which is counted as raw gas-phase particles rather than equivalent electrons. It is directly parallel to same-family species quantities such as [argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), differing by the injected species and its atomic number.

rows.name: nuclear_power_density_of_limiter_tile
rows.source_description: Nuclear power density heating this unit evaluated at the midplane (whenever relevant)
rows.documentation:
Nuclear power density of a limiter tile is the local volumetric energy deposition rate within the material of one limiter tile caused by neutron interactions and associated gamma-radiation absorption. It is the nuclear contribution to the broader [power density of a limiter tile], not the total local energy source.

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{tile}}} q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the nuclear power density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{tile}}$ is the material volume of the limiter tile, and $P_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the corresponding [nuclear power of a limiter tile](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_limiter_tile).

The quantity includes energy deposited volumetrically by neutron scattering and capture and by absorption of primary and secondary gamma radiation. Surface heat loads, externally applied heating, and nonnuclear energy-transfer mechanisms are excluded.

rows.name: perpendicular_power_normalized_of_beam_tracing_beam
rows.source_description: Normalized power flow in the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the magnitude of the local time-averaged electromagnetic power-flow component perpendicular to the local magnetic-field direction, normalized by the beam’s initial launch power. It measures transverse power flow and is not a signed projection onto a selected perpendicular direction.

$$
p_{\perp} = \frac{\left\lVert \mathbf{P} - (\mathbf{P}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}})\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right\rVert}{P_0}
$$

where $\mathbf{P}$ is the local beam power-flow vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, and $P_0$ is the initial launch power. The magnitude makes $p_{\perp}$ non-negative. Together with the signed [parallel normalized beam power], it characterizes the local power-flow decomposition relative to the magnetic field; [initial beam power](name:initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam) supplies the normalization reference.

rows.name: lithium_density_at_limiter
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
Lithium density at a limiter is the local number density of lithium ions in the boundary plasma immediately adjacent to a plasma-facing limiter surface. The evaluation point is on the plasma side of the magnetic presheath or sheath entrance.

$$
n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{r}_L)=\frac{dN_{\mathrm{Li}}}{dV}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $N_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the counted number of lithium ions, $V$ is volume in m$^3$, and $\mathbf{r}_L$ is the evaluation position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius in m, $\phi$ is toroidal angle in radians, and $Z$ is vertical height in m.

The quantity is summed over all positive lithium ionization states and excludes neutral lithium atoms. It is the lithium-specific specialization of [density at a limiter](name:density_at_limiter) and differs from the broader [ion density at a limiter], which does not select lithium.

rows.name: total_gas_source_rate_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
Gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection is the instantaneous total unweighted source rate of neutral gas particles injected by gas-injection valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane. It counts injected neutral gas particles themselves, not electron-equivalent particles, charge-weighted particles, or particles produced by later plasma or wall interactions.

For the set of midplane injection valves, the total rate is the sum of the individual unweighted valve particle throughputs:

$$
\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}} \dot{N}_k
$$

where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{mid}}^{\mathrm{gas\,inj}}$ is the gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is the set of gas-injection valves assigned to the vessel equatorial midplane, and $\dot{N}_k$ is the unweighted neutral-particle throughput of valve $k$.

The total includes all gas-injection valves in the midplane group and excludes upper, lower, wall, recycling, pumping, ionization, and transport contributions. It is not additive with regional gas-source quantities that use an electron-equivalent or charge-weighted convention. Its time integral is the corresponding [accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas injection].

rows.name: vertical_vorticity
rows.source_description: Component along the height axis, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Vertical vorticity is the component of the plasma vorticity vector along the vertical direction. It measures the signed local rotation of the bulk plasma flow in the horizontal plane and is one directional projection of [vorticity](name:vorticity).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the defining relation is:

$$
\omega_Z = \boldsymbol{\omega}\cdot\hat{Z} = (\nabla\times\mathbf{v})\cdot\hat{Z}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}$ is the local bulk plasma velocity in m/s, $\boldsymbol{\omega}$ is the vorticity vector in s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector. Here $R$ is major radius in m, $\phi$ is toroidal angle in radians, and $Z$ is vertical height in m.

The related [toroidal vorticity](name:toroidal_vorticity) projects the same vorticity vector onto $\hat{\phi}$ instead. The major-radius-scaled quantity [vertical vorticity divided by major radius](name:ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius) is distinct because it includes an additional inverse-length factor.

Sign convention: Positive when the bulk velocity field rotates in the right-hand sense about the positive vertical direction $+\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

Related quantities: [radial_vorticity](name:radial_vorticity).

rows.name: total_thermal_ion_heat_flux
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the thermal-energy flux density carried across an oriented surface by all ion species and their charge states. It combines conductive transport with convective transport of thermal enthalpy.

The surface-normal component is defined by

$$
q_{i,n} = \mathbf{q}_i \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}} = \left(\mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}
$$

where $\mathbf{q}_i$ is the [total ion energy flux](name:total_ion_energy_flux) vector, $\mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{cond}}$ and $\mathbf{q}_{i,\mathrm{conv}}$ are its conductive and convective thermal components, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the oriented surface-normal unit vector. The ion sum excludes electron, electromagnetic, fast-ion, neutral, and directed bulk kinetic-energy fluxes.

Sign convention: Positive when ion thermal energy is transported in the direction of the oriented surface normal.

rows.name: vertical_back_surface_curvature_of_optical_element
rows.source_description: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5
rows.documentation:
Vertical back-surface curvature of an optical element is the signed directional radius of curvature of the back optical surface in its second local tangential aperture direction. The right-handed local optical-surface frame is $(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1, \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2, \hat{\mathbf{n}}_b)$ with $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1 \times \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2 = \hat{\mathbf{n}}_b$, where $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ are the first and second surface-tangential aperture directions and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_b$ is the positive normal of the back surface; this quantity uses $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$, the object-local aperture vertical direction.

The defining relation is the reciprocal of the signed normal curvature of the back-surface normal section tangent to $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$:

$$
R_{b,2} = \frac{1}{\kappa_{n,b}(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2)}
$$

where $R_{b,2}$ is the vertical back-surface curvature of the optical element and $\kappa_{n,b}(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2)$ is the signed normal curvature of the back surface in the $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ direction.

This is a local directional radius, not the scalar parent [optical-element curvature] and not the direction-agnostic [back-surface curvature]. It equals the first-direction radius only for locally spherical or otherwise direction-independent curvature, and it is not a principal, sagittal, or meridional radius unless the surface definition aligns $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ with that direction. Together with an orthogonal directional radius it may characterize simple aligned toroidal curvature, but it does not fully characterize a general aspherical surface.

rows.name: ion_average_temperature_at_post_sawtooth_crash
rows.source_description: Ion temperature (averaged on charge states and ion species)
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the energy-equivalent temperature of the ion population after a sawtooth crash, averaged over every included ion species and charge state. It characterizes the mean thermal energy of the post-crash ions and is distinct from a temperature assigned to one species or charge state.

$$
T_i = \frac{\sum_s n_s T_s}{\sum_s n_s}
$$

where $T_i$ is the averaged ion temperature, $T_s$ is the temperature of ion species and charge state $s$, and $n_s$ is its number density. The summation includes all ion species and charge states in the defined population. The corresponding general quantity is [ion average temperature](name:ion_average_temperature), while [ion average temperature at an internal transport barrier](name:ion_average_temperature_at_internal_transport_barrier) applies the same averaging concept at a different plasma locus.

rows.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
The ion charge-state particle flux limiter coefficient sets the maximum permitted particle-flux density for one specified ionization charge state relative to its free-streaming bound.

$$
\left\lVert \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s} \right\rVert \leq f_s \left\lVert \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{fs},s} \right\rVert
$$

where $f_s$ is the flux limiter coefficient, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{s}$ is the particle flux density of the specified ion charge state, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{\mathrm{fs},s}$ is its free-streaming particle-flux bound, and $\lVert\cdot\rVert$ denotes vector magnitude.

The coefficient applies to particle transport for the selected ion charge state, including thermal and nonthermal contributions when represented. It is not summed over ion charge states and does not limit energy or momentum transport. The corresponding [ion charge-state particle flux](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux) is the bounded vector quantity; this coefficient is not itself a flux. The particle-channel limitation is distinct from the [ion momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), which applies to momentum transport.

rows.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_hard_xray_detector
rows.source_description: Positions along x2 axis
rows.documentation:
Second local tangential coordinate of a hard X-ray detector is the signed scalar coordinate of a detector outline vertex along the detector-local second tangential direction. It is defined in the right-handed object-local Cartesian basis $(\hat{\mathbf e}_1, \hat{\mathbf e}_2, \hat{\mathbf e}_3)$, where $\hat{\mathbf e}_1$ is the first local tangential unit vector, $\hat{\mathbf e}_3$ is the detector-local normal unit vector, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_2 = \hat{\mathbf e}_3 \times \hat{\mathbf e}_1$.

The coordinate $q_2$ of a vertex at position $\mathbf r$ is the signed projection of its displacement from the detector-local origin:

$$
q_2 = (\mathbf r - \mathbf r_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_2
$$

where $\mathbf r_0$ is the detector-local origin and $\hat{\mathbf e}_2$ is the second local tangential unit vector.

Only the component along $\hat{\mathbf e}_2$ is included. The companion coordinate along $\hat{\mathbf e}_1$ is the [first local tangential coordinate of a hard X-ray detector]; neither quantity is a radial, toroidal, or vertical component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement from the detector-local origin is toward $\hat{\mathbf e}_3 \times \hat{\mathbf e}_1$.

rows.name: line_averaged_tungsten_density
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the line-of-sight average of the charge-state-summed number density of positively charged tungsten ions.

$$
\bar n_{\mathrm{W}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{L}} \left[\sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)\right] \, dl
$$

Here, $\bar n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the line-averaged tungsten-ion number density, $\mathcal{L}$ is the specified averaging line, $L$ is its total length, $l$ is distance along that line, $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)$ is the local number density of tungsten ions in charge state $Z$. The sum includes all positive tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten.

The quantity applies to the aggregate tungsten-ion population along the specified line and is averaged over that line rather than evaluated locally or averaged over volume. It therefore differs from the local or otherwise spatially averaged [tungsten-ion density](name:tungsten_density) by its line-of-sight aggregation, and from [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density) by using a line rather than the enclosed plasma volume.

rows.name: electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping
rows.source_description: Pumped particle flux (in equivalent electrons)
rows.documentation:
The rate at which particles of the electron-equivalent population are removed from the plasma region by wall pumping is the global scalar representation of the wall particle-removal flux. It describes pumped particle exhaust using equivalent-electron counting rather than a local wall flux density.

The global removal rate is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{pump}} = \frac{dN_{e,\mathrm{removed}}}{dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{pump}}$ is the pumped particle-removal rate expressed in equivalent electrons, $N_{e,\mathrm{removed}}$ is the cumulative number of electron equivalents removed by wall pumping, and $t$ is time.

This quantity is aggregated over the wall and represents the total pumping throughput for the electron-equivalent population. The electron-equivalent basis does not assert that all removed particles are physical electrons, and the quantity is not an areal flux density, an electrical current, or a rate for one specified neutral species.

It is the electron-specific specialization of the general [particle-removal flux at the wall due to pumping](name:particle_rate_at_wall_due_to_pumping). In contrast, [neutral particle flux at the wall due to pumping](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping) uses a specified neutral species as its counting population rather than equivalent-electron counting.

rows.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_filter_window
rows.source_description: Full width of the filter in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type/index = 3
rows.documentation:
The quantity is the complete physical aperture extent of a filter window along its first local tangential direction, denoted by $X_1$. It defines the opening available for radiation transmission, not a material thickness or spectral bandwidth.

For a rectangular opening, the full width is the separation of its opposing boundaries along $X_1$:

$$
w_1 = x_{1,\max} - x_{1,\min}
$$

where $w_1$ is the full first-direction width, and $x_{1,\max}$ and $x_{1,\min}$ are the positions of the two opposing filter-window boundaries along $X_1$.

This quantity applies only when the filter window has rectangular geometry. It is the complete boundary-to-boundary extent for one filter window along its first local tangential direction, with no spatial, spectral, or population aggregation. It is not a half-width, a second-direction width, a radius, a material thickness, or a spectral bandwidth.

The first-direction width is one dimension of the rectangular clear opening that admits radiation; the complementary second-direction extent is a separate geometric quantity. For a circular filter window, the corresponding size distinction is represented by its [filter-window radius](name:radius_of_filter_window), while the same first-direction width concept for another rectangular optical opening is represented by the [first local tangential width of a diagnostic aperture](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_diagnostic_aperture).

rows.name: toroidal_magnetic_field_at_flux_surface
rows.source_description: Toroidal component of the magnetic field
rows.documentation:
Toroidal magnetic field at a flux surface is the coefficient $B_\phi$ multiplying $\hat{\phi}$ in the cylindrical decomposition of the equilibrium magnetic-field vector at a point on a selected magnetic flux surface. The direction $\hat{\phi}$ belongs to the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ basis, where $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$.

The component is the signed scalar projection onto the toroidal basis vector:

$$
B_\phi(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\phi}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the point on the selected magnetic flux surface and $\mathbf{B}$ is the equilibrium magnetic-field vector.

This is the cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ toroidal component, not the [poloidal magnetic field at a flux surface], [radial magnetic field at a flux surface], [vertical magnetic field at a flux surface], or [magnetic-field magnitude at a flux surface]. The surface locus is specified independently, for example by the [poloidal magnetic flux at a flux surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface); this quantity is not the flux label itself.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic-field vector component is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: tungsten_density_flux_surface_averaged_at_plasma_boundary
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the number density of tungsten ions averaged over the last closed magnetic flux surface, with all positive ionization states included and neutral tungsten excluded. It is the surface-averaged counterpart of the local [tungsten density at the plasma boundary](name:tungsten_density_flux_surface_averaged_at_plasma_boundary).

The flux-surface average at the plasma-boundary flux label is defined by

$$
\langle n_{\mathrm{W}} \rangle_{\psi_b} = \frac{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} n_{\mathrm{W}}\,d\ell_p/B_p}{\oint_{\psi=\psi_b} d\ell_p/B_p}
$$

where $\psi_b$ is the flux label of the plasma boundary, $n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the local summed tungsten-ion density, $d\ell_p$ is poloidal contour length, and $B_p$ is the poloidal magnetic-field magnitude. The quantity is distinct from [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density), which averages over the enclosed plasma volume.

rows.name: current_of_divertor_tile
rows.source_description: Total current incident on this tile
rows.documentation:
Conventional electric current of a divertor tile is the net signed charge current crossing the electrostatic sheath from the plasma onto the plasma-facing surface of one individual divertor tile. It is a tile-level incident sheath current, expressed using the direction of conventional electric current rather than electron particle flow.

The current is the sheath-normal surface integral of the conventional electric current density over the tile surface:

$$
I_\mathrm{tile} = \int_{S_\mathrm{tile}} \mathbf{j} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{tile}} \, dS
$$

where $I_\mathrm{tile}$ is the conventional electric current of the divertor tile, $S_\mathrm{tile}$ is the plasma-facing surface of that tile, $\mathbf{j}$ is the conventional electric current density, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{p}\to\mathrm{tile}}$ is the surface normal directed from the plasma toward the tile, and $dS$ is the surface-area element.

The scope is one individual divertor tile and the aggregation is the net charge-weighted contribution of all charged species crossing the sheath onto that tile surface. It is not the current of a complete divertor target, not the current of an entire divertor, and not an electrical-conduction current in supports or external circuitry after charge has entered the solid.

The [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target) is obtained by summing this quantity over the divertor tiles that constitute that target. The [current of a divertor](name:current_of_divertor) is obtained by summing the corresponding tile or target contributions over the divertor.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional electric current crosses the electrostatic sheath from the plasma toward the plasma-facing surface of the divertor tile.

rows.name: line_averaged_lithium_density
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
This is the path-length average of lithium ion number density, summed over all ionization stages from Li$^+$ through fully stripped Li$^{3+}$, along a specified chord through the plasma.

The chord average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{Li} \rangle_L = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_{Li}(s)\,ds
$$

where $n_{Li}(s)$ is the local lithium ion number density in m$^{-3}$, $s$ is path length in meters along the chord, and $L$ is the total chord length in meters.

This quantity weights each path-length element equally and excludes neutral lithium. It differs from the [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary], which averages over a separatrix, and from [volume-averaged lithium density](name:volume_averaged_lithium_density), which averages over confined plasma volume.

rows.name: hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
Hydrogen ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local count of hydrogen ions per unit volume at the pedestal's core-side shoulder. It is specific to hydrogen ions rather than the total ion population.

The charge-state-summed hydrogen ion density is defined by:

$$
n_{\mathrm H} = \sum_{Z\geq 1} n_{\mathrm H}^{(Z+)}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm H}$ is the local hydrogen-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm H}^{(Z+)}$ is the local number density of hydrogen ions with charge state $Z+$, and $Z$ is the positive integer charge-state index.

This quantity applies locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). The aggregation is a sum over all hydrogen ion charge states; neutral hydrogen and ions of other elements are excluded.

It differs from [flux-surface-averaged hydrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which is averaged over a flux surface and evaluated at the plasma boundary, and from [hydrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:hydrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which has a different spatial locus.

rows.name: power_due_to_first_orbit_loss
rows.source_description: Power loss due to first orbit losses
rows.documentation:
First-orbit-loss power is the kinetic-energy loss rate carried away by fast ions whose first guiding-center orbit after birth or acceleration intersects the confining boundary. It represents the aggregate loss from the confined fast-ion population, rather than energy transferred by collisions or subsequent orbit evolution.

The volume-integrated loss power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{FOL}} = \int_V p_{\mathrm{FOL}}^{(1)}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{FOL}}$ is the first-orbit-loss power, $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $p_{\mathrm{FOL}}^{(1)}$ is the local kinetic-energy loss rate density from first-orbit-unconfined fast ions.

The quantity is a non-negative loss magnitude and excludes power losses specifically attributed to charge exchange, such as [fast-ion power due to charge exchange](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_charge_exchange).

rows.name: poloidal_total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the effective diffusivity governing diffusive transport of the aggregate bulk-flow momentum in the local poloidal direction within the edge plasma.

Its relation to the directional momentum-diffusivity tensor is

$$
D_{\mathrm{pol}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}} \cdot \mathbf D_{\mathrm{mom}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}
$$

where $D_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the poloidal diffusion coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the local unit vector in the poloidal direction, and $\mathbf D_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is the effective diffusivity tensor for total bulk-flow momentum; the dot products denote tensor contraction.

The total designation means that this coefficient applies to the aggregate momentum balance without selecting an ion species, ion charge state, or neutral state. It is restricted to the poloidal transport direction and the edge-plasma region; it does not represent a species-resolved coefficient or a coefficient for another transport direction.

This quantity is the poloidal component of the directional coefficient vector represented by [total momentum diffusion coefficient](name:total_momentum_diffusion_coefficient). It is distinct from [poloidal ion momentum diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient), which applies only to ion momentum transport, and from [poloidal neutral-state momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_diffusivity), which applies only to neutral-state momentum transport.

rows.name: pedestal_thermal_ion_energy
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the total thermal energy stored by the ion populations throughout the H-mode pedestal region. It is an extensive quantity obtained by integrating the local ion thermal energy density over the full pedestal volume.

The defining relation is

$$
W_{\mathrm{ped},i} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{ped}}} \frac{3}{2} p_i(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{ped},i}$ is the pedestal thermal ion energy, $V_{\mathrm{ped}}$ is the pedestal volume, $p_i(\mathbf{x})$ is the total local thermal pressure of the ion populations, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is a volume element. The factor $3/2$ applies to an isotropic thermal pressure.

The integral aggregates all thermal ion species and charge states included in $p_i$ over the complete pedestal region. It excludes electron thermal energy, nonthermal particle energy, bulk-flow kinetic energy, magnetic energy, and other energy forms. It is a volume-integrated energy, not the local ion temperature at the pedestal top represented by [ion average temperature at pedestal top](name:ion_average_temperature_at_pedestal_top).

The corresponding electron contribution is a distinct quantity: [pedestal thermal electron energy](name:pedestal_thermal_electron_energy) applies the same volume-integrated thermal-energy concept to electrons rather than ions.

rows.name: volume_integrated_particle_source_rate
rows.source_description: Source rate of thermal particles due to the thermalization of fast particles
rows.documentation:
The volume-integrated particle source rate is the net rate at which particles are added to or removed from a specified distribution throughout the plasma volume.

It is defined from the local particle source rate density by

$$
\mathcal{S}_p = \int_V s_p(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_p$ is the volume-integrated particle source rate, $s_p(\mathbf{x})$ is the local net particle source rate density, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $V$ is the represented plasma volume, $dV$ is the volume element, and the subscript $p$ identifies the particle channel.

The quantity applies to the particular distribution or source represented and does not impose a species, charge-state, or thermal-population restriction. Its aggregation is the spatial integral over the full represented plasma volume; no additional sum over species or charge states is implied. External particle injection, wave-particle interaction, and transfer between nonthermal and thermal populations may contribute when they define the underlying source.

This global rate is distinct from the local [thermal particle source rate](name:thermal_particle_source_rate), which is restricted to the thermal population, and from the local [ion-state source rate](name:ion_state_source_rate), which is resolved for one ion charge state. Positive values represent net entry into the represented distribution, while negative values represent net removal; a thermalization contribution can therefore be negative when particles leave the thermal population.

rows.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
rows.source_description: Component along Y axis  for each voxel
rows.documentation:
Y direction unit-vector component of a neutron detector is the signed projection, in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, of the unit vector directed from a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center. It is the y direction cosine of that line-of-sight direction.

The component is defined by projecting the detector-directed unit vector onto the $\hat{y}$ basis vector:

$$
u_y = \hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}} \cdot \hat{y} = \frac{(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}) \cdot \hat{y}}{\lVert \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}} - \mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}} \rVert}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{u}}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the unit vector from the field-of-view voxel center to the detector center, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{det}}$ is the detector-center position, $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{vox}}$ is the field-of-view voxel-center position, and $\hat{y}$ is the y basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame.

This quantity is a signed direction-cosine component, not a position coordinate, distance, or unnormalized displacement component. Together with the corresponding x and z components it satisfies $u_x^2 + u_y^2 + u_z^2 = 1$ when the field-of-view voxel center and detector center are distinct.

rows.name: radial_neutral_particle_convection_velocity
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Radial neutral-particle convection velocity is the effective coefficient of the density-proportional advective flux of neutral particles in edge-plasma transport. It represents directed drift, pinch, or outward convection after density-gradient-driven diffusive transport has been separated.

The radial convective particle flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{n,r}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_n v_{n,r}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial particle flux due to convection, $n_n$ is the neutral-particle number density, and $v_{n,r}$ is this radial convection velocity.

The quantity applies to the neutral-particle channel in the edge plasma and is the radial component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is an effective coefficient for the named neutral-particle population, not a sum of energy or momentum transport coefficients.

The quantity excludes density-gradient-driven diffusive transport and is distinct from the full [neutral_particle_convection_velocity](name:neutral_particle_convection_velocity), which has no directional projection. The [parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity](name:parallel_neutral_particle_convection_velocity) represents the corresponding projection along the magnetic field rather than along increasing major radius.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral-particle convective velocity points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: second_local_tangential_back_surface_radius_of_optical_element
rows.source_description: Radius of curvature in the X2 direction, to be filled only for curvature_type/index = 3 or 5
rows.documentation:
Second local tangential (X2) back-surface radius of curvature of an optical element is the signed directional radius of curvature of the element's back surface in the surface-normal section whose tangent is the second object-local tangential direction. It characterizes the local surface figure of that back face when the back surface is curved.

The directional radius is the reciprocal of the signed normal curvature in the same surface direction:

$$
R_{2,\mathrm{back}} = \frac{1}{\kappa_{2,\mathrm{back}}}
$$

where $R_{2,\mathrm{back}}$ is the second local tangential back-surface radius of curvature of the optical element and $\kappa_{2,\mathrm{back}}$ is the signed normal curvature of the optical-element back surface in the same second object-local tangential direction.

The quantity applies to one optical element and to its back surface only. It is defined only for curved back-surface types for which a second local tangential radius is specified; it is not a planar-surface parameter, not an average over surfaces, optical elements, or tangential directions, and not a radius along any machine-fixed axis.

The [first local tangential back-surface radius of an optical element](name:first_local_tangential_back_surface_radius_of_optical_element) is the corresponding radius on the same back surface along the orthogonal first object-local tangential direction. The [second local tangential front-surface radius of an optical element](name:second_local_tangential_front_surface_radius_of_optical_element) is the opposite-surface counterpart along the same second object-local tangential direction. In optical-element surface names that use vertical for this surface direction, such as [vertical back-surface curvature of an optical element](name:vertical_back_surface_curvature_of_optical_element) and [vertical front-surface radius of an optical element](name:vertical_front_surface_radius_of_optical_element), vertical denotes the same object-local second tangential direction, not a machine-fixed direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the center of curvature of the back-surface normal section in the second local tangential direction lies in the direction of the oriented local normal of the back surface.

rows.name: toroidal_impurity_ion_velocity_at_measurement_position
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
The quantity is the impurity-ion bulk-flow velocity projected onto the toroidal direction at the specified measurement position. It is a signed velocity component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
v_\phi(\mathbf{x}_m)=\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{imp}}(\mathbf{x}_m)\cdot\hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_\phi$ is the toroidal velocity component, $\mathbf{x}_m$ is the measurement position, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the bulk velocity of the impurity-ion population, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

For an impurity population combined over charge states, the bulk velocity is the density-weighted mean over the included charge states. The species and charge-state aggregation must be interpreted from the defined population; the related [toroidal ion velocity](name:toroidal_ion_velocity) provides the corresponding generic ion quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the impurity-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: resistance_of_correction_coil
rows.source_description: Coil resistance
rows.documentation:
The resistance of a non-axisymmetric correction-coil conductor is the proportionality between its steady conventional current and the associated ohmic voltage drop. It describes dissipation in the conductor rather than inductive or other reactive voltage contributions.

For a uniform conductor, the resistance is defined by

$$
R = \rho \frac{L}{A}
$$

where $R$ is resistance in ohms, $\rho$ is electrical resistivity in ohm-meters, $L$ is the effective conductor length in meters, and $A$ is the cross-sectional area in square meters. The terminal relation is $V = IR$, where $V$ is the ohmic voltage drop and $I$ is the current; the corresponding resistive power is $P = I^2R$. The current is the [current of the correction coil], and the conductor area is represented by the [area of the correction coil](name:area_of_correction_coil).

rows.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
rows.source_description: Imaginary part
rows.documentation:
Imaginary part of the radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the imaginary component of the complex first-order magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the confined plasma. It applies to one toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis and to the radial coordinate component in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

The complex radial component is decomposed into real and imaginary parts as:

$$
\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) = \delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) + i\,\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta)
$$

where $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$ is the radial flux-coordinate component of the complex perturbed magnetic-field eigenfunction for toroidal mode number $n$, $\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}$ is the corresponding [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), $\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ is this quantity, $i$ is the imaginary unit, $\rho$ is the radial flux coordinate, and $\theta$ is the poloidal flux coordinate.

The scope is the confined-plasma region for the specified toroidal mode; it excludes the perturbed magnetic field in the vacuum region, any sum over toroidal mode numbers, and any real-valued instantaneous perturbation obtained after applying a toroidal and temporal phase factor. The radial direction here is the coordinate direction associated with increasing $\rho$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$; it is distinct from the major-radius $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity is a local eigenfunction component, not a flux-surface average, volume integral, or magnitude.

Together with the [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), this quantity forms the complex radial component $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$. Together with the [poloidal](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) and [toroidal](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) imaginary components, it forms the imaginary vector part of the perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction. The overall complex phase of a linear eigenfunction is arbitrary, so a phase rotation mixes the real and imaginary parts while leaving the represented complex eigenfunction unchanged.

Sign convention: Positive when the imaginary radial component points toward increasing radial flux coordinate $\rho$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ for the adopted complex eigenfunction phase.

rows.name: polarization_angle_at_constraint_position
rows.source_description: Measured value
rows.documentation:
The polarization angle at a constraint position is the angle of linear polarization of Stark-split Balmer-alpha emission from fast neutral beam ions traversing the plasma, evaluated at a discrete spatial site where this measurement serves as an input constraint in equilibrium reconstruction. The motional Stark effect (MSE) diagnostic exploits the Lorentz electric field experienced by injected beam neutrals to align the polarization plane of the emitted light in a direction encoding the local magnetic-field pitch angle.

The MSE polarization angle $\gamma$ is related to the local magnetic field components by:

$$
\tan(\gamma) = \frac{B_Z}{A_1 B_R + A_2 B_\phi}
$$

where $B_Z$ is the vertical field component, $B_R$ is the radial field component, $B_\phi$ is the toroidal field component, and $A_1$, $A_2$ are dimensionless geometric weighting factors determined by the beam trajectory and sightline orientation.

During equilibrium reconstruction, the measured value at each constraint position is compared against the corresponding reconstructed [polarization_angle](name:polarization_angle_at_constraint_position) to form residuals that enter the least-squares cost functional. The motional_stark_radiance provides complementary spectral intensity data from the same beam-emission event. MSE polarization angles in conventional-aspect-ratio tokamak configurations span a few degrees to roughly 20 degrees, varying with local field pitch, beam geometry, and viewing-sightline angle.

rows.name: nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer
rows.source_description: Nuclear power heating this layer
rows.documentation:
Nuclear heating power of a breeder-blanket layer is the volume-integrated rate at which neutron and photon interactions convert radiation energy into heat within that material layer. It is the nuclear component of [heating power of a breeder-blanket layer], rather than the local volumetric quantity [nuclear power density of a breeder-blanket layer](name:nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_layer).

The defining relation is

$$
P_{\mathrm{nuc,layer}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{layer}}} \dot{q}_{\mathrm{nuc}}\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{nuc,layer}}$ is the layer-integrated nuclear heating power, $\dot{q}_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the local nuclear energy-deposition rate per unit volume, and $V_{\mathrm{layer}}$ is the volume of the specified material layer.

The integral includes energy deposited by neutron interactions and absorption of primary or secondary photons within the layer. It excludes plasma-facing radiative heat loads, incident energy that is not deposited, and energy deposited outside the layer; the result is non-negative.

rows.name: parallel_fast_particle_pressure
rows.source_description: Pressure of fast particles in the parallel direction
rows.documentation:
Parallel fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned component of the kinetic pressure tensor carried by suprathermal particles. It is the all-orbit contribution to [fast-particle pressure], complementary to the transverse [perpendicular fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure).

The flux-surface-averaged pressure is defined by the parallel second velocity moment:

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}(\psi)=\left\langle \sum_s m_s\int v_\parallel^2 f_{\mathrm{fast},s}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\right\rangle_\psi
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $\langle\cdot\rangle_\psi$ denotes its flux-surface average, $s$ labels fast-particle species, $m_s$ is particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity, $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{b}$ is velocity along the magnetic-field unit vector $\mathbf{b}$, and $f_{\mathrm{fast},s}$ is the distribution function.

All guiding-center orbit classes are included, including co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped particles. The associated scalar trace satisfies $P_{\mathrm{fast}}=(P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fast}}+2P_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}})/3$; an orbit-restricted counterpart is [parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure).

rows.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
rows.source_description: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
The toroidal ion charge-state momentum convection velocity is the $\phi$-component of the effective velocity vector $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ appearing in the non-diffusive term of the charge-state-resolved fluid momentum transport equation for ion charge state $s$:

$$
v_{c,\phi}^{(s)} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}
$$

where $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and $\mathbf{v}_c^{(s)}$ is the effective momentum convection velocity vector for charge state $s$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and is distinct from [toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity), which provides the corresponding quantity aggregated over all charge states of a species. It is one projection component of the [ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) vector family. As a transport coefficient in a convection-diffusion closure, it is not in general equal to the mean toroidal fluid velocity of the charge state.

Sign convention: Positive when $v_{c,\phi}^{(s)}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of oxygen atoms admitted after plasma breakdown through gas injection, converted to an equivalent-electron count. Each oxygen atom contributes eight equivalent electrons, corresponding to oxygen's atomic number.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 8N_{\mathrm{O}}(t) = 8\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the cumulative oxygen-atom count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{O}}$ is the oxygen-atom injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation time. The count quantities are dimensionless and the injection rate has units of inverse seconds.

Only oxygen delivered after plasma breakdown by gas injection is included; prefill oxygen is excluded and is represented by accumulated_oxygen_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection. The instantaneous counterpart is [oxygen_source_rate](name:oxygen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), while accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection uses the corresponding atomic-number weighting for carbon.

rows.name: alpha_angle_of_plasma_filament
rows.source_description: Inclination of first angle measured counter-clockwise from horizontal outwardly directed radial vector (grad R).
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the signed inclination of the first side of the oblique parallelogram representing an individual plasma-filament cross section. It specifies the orientation of that side in the poloidal plane relative to the outward radial direction.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the angle is defined by

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}\left(\mathbf{a}_1\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_Z,\,\mathbf{a}_1\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_R\right)
$$

where $\alpha$ is the first-side inclination, $\mathbf{a}_1$ is the directed vector along the first parallelogram side, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_R$ is the outward radial unit vector in the direction of increasing $R$, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_Z$ is the positive vertical unit vector, and $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the signed angle from the radial projection toward the vertical projection.

The quantity applies separately to each discrete plasma-carrying filament and is not an aggregate orientation averaged over the plasma. It describes only the first side of the oblique cross section; it is not the inclination of the second side or either side length.

The companion [tilt angle of a plasma filament](name:tilt_angle_of_plasma_filament) specifies the inclination of the other parallelogram side, while the [major length of a plasma filament](name:major_length_of_plasma_filament) and [minor length of a plasma filament](name:minor_length_of_plasma_filament) specify cross-sectional dimensions. Together these geometric quantities define the filament cross-section orientation and shape.

Sign convention: Positive when the directed first side is rotated counterclockwise from the outward radial direction toward the positive vertical direction in the poloidal plane.

rows.name: parallel_power_normalized_of_beam_tracing_beam
rows.source_description: Normalized power flow in the direction parallel to the magnetic field
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the signed local fraction of electromagnetic power carried by a coherent beam-tracing beam in the direction parallel to the local magnetic field. It is evaluated along the beam’s ray path and referenced to the beam’s initial launched power.

The normalized parallel fraction is defined by

$$
f_\parallel = \frac{P_\parallel}{P_0} = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{A}} \langle\mathbf{S}\rangle \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}\,\mathrm{d}A}{P_0}
$$

where $P_\parallel$ is the local parallel power flow, $\langle\mathbf{S}\rangle$ is the time-averaged electromagnetic Poynting vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $\mathcal{A}$ is the beam cross-section, and $P_0$ is the [initial power of the beam-tracing beam](name:initial_power_of_beam_tracing_beam). This signed projection is distinct from the non-negative [perpendicular normalized power of the beam-tracing beam](name:perpendicular_power_normalized_of_beam_tracing_beam).

Sign convention: Positive when the local electromagnetic power flow has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

rows.name: ratio_of_vertical_vorticity_to_major_radius
rows.source_description: Component along the height axis, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the major-radius-scaled form of [vertical vorticity](name:vertical_vorticity), measuring local bulk-plasma rotation about the vertical direction per unit major radius. It is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\omega_Z^*(R,\phi,Z)=\frac{\omega_Z(R,\phi,Z)}{R},\qquad \omega_Z=(\nabla\times\mathbf{v})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, $\mathbf{v}$ is the plasma bulk-velocity vector, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The scaling applies to the vertical-vorticity component itself and does not represent the full [vorticity](name:vorticity) vector.

Sign convention: Positive when the bulk-flow rotation is in the $+Z$ sense, namely counterclockwise in the $(R,\phi)$ plane when viewed from $+Z$.

rows.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
Toroidal helium-4 velocity at the magnetic axis is the signed bulk-flow velocity of helium-4 ions projected onto the toroidal basis vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame at the magnetic axis. As a species-level velocity, it is the density-weighted mean over all charge states of helium-4 present at that locus.

The scalar projection is defined by:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{He}^4,\mathrm{axis}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He}^4,\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He}^4,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the density-weighted mean helium-4 bulk-flow velocity vector at the magnetic axis and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal basis vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

This quantity is localized to the magnetic axis and is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal helium-4 velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary). It is species-specific to helium-4 and is distinct from [toroidal helium-3 velocity at the magnetic axis](name:toroidal_helium_3_velocity_at_magnetic_axis).

rows.name: toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_pedestal_top
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
The carbon impurity-ion fluid velocity at the H-mode pedestal top is the density-weighted bulk-flow velocity of all contributing carbon ion charge states, evaluated at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It is the toroidal component rather than the total three-dimensional speed, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

$$
v_{\phi,C}=\frac{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}v_{\phi,C^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{C^{q+}}}
$$

Here, $q$ indexes the contributing carbon ion charge states, $n_{C^{q+}}$ is the corresponding number density in m$^{-3}$, and $v_{\phi,C^{q+}}$ is its toroidal velocity in m s$^{-1}$. Neutral carbon is excluded because this quantity is defined for impurity ions. The pedestal-top value is distinct from the [toroidal carbon velocity at the plasma boundary](name:toroidal_carbon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the carbon-ion flow has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

rows.name: poloidal_neutral_energy_diffusivity
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Poloidal neutral energy diffusivity is the effective diagonal transport coefficient for diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by neutral atoms and molecules along the poloidal direction.

In flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, its defining constitutive relation is

$$
q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}=-D_{n,\theta}\frac{\partial u_n}{\partial s_\theta}
$$

where $q_{n,\theta}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the poloidal diffusive neutral-energy flux density, $D_{n,\theta}$ is the poloidal diffusivity, $u_n$ is neutral thermal-energy density, and $s_\theta$ is physical arclength along the poloidal tangent at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$. The diffusivity has units of m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, while $s_\theta$ is measured in m.

This quantity is the poloidal specialization of [neutral energy diffusivity](name:effective_neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient). It aggregates the relevant neutral populations and is distinct from the state-resolved [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity).

rows.name: poloidal_electron_energy_flux
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Poloidal electron energy flux is the directed flux of electron thermal energy and enthalpy per unit area along the direction of increasing poloidal angle in flux coordinates $(\\psi,\\theta,\\phi)$. It is the poloidal projection of the net [electron energy flux](name:electron_energy_flux), including conductive and convective transport.

The defining projection is

$$
q_{e,\\theta} = \\mathbf{q}_e \\cdot \\hat{\\boldsymbol{e}}_\\theta
$$

where $q_{e,\\theta}$ is the poloidal electron energy flux, $\\mathbf{q}_e$ is the electron energy-flux vector, and $\\hat{\\boldsymbol{e}}_\\theta$ is the unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\\theta$ on a surface of constant $\\psi$.

This directional component is distinct from the [radial electron energy flux](name:radial_electron_energy_flux), which is projected along the cylindrical $+R$ direction; together they describe different projections of the parent vector quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the electron energy flux points toward increasing poloidal angle $\\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\\psi,\\theta,\\phi)$.

rows.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_soft_xray_detector
rows.source_description: Full width of the aperture in the X1 direction, used only if geometry_type = 3
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the full end-to-end width of a soft X-ray detector's rectangular aperture along its object-local first tangential axis, denoted X1. It defines one dimension of the detector acceptance geometry used in etendue calculations.

The width is defined by

$$
w_1 = x_{1,\mathrm{max}} - x_{1,\mathrm{min}}
$$

where $w_1$ is the first-local-tangential aperture width, and $x_{1,\mathrm{max}}$ and $x_{1,\mathrm{min}}$ are the coordinates of the two opposing aperture boundaries along X1.

The quantity applies to one soft X-ray detector aperture with rectangular geometry and represents the complete boundary-to-boundary extent, not a half-width, an outline coordinate, the second local tangential width, or an aggregate over multiple detectors. The boundary coordinates used in the defining difference are provided by the [first local tangential coordinate of the soft X-ray detector](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_soft_xray_detector). The same geometric convention is used for the corresponding [first local tangential width of a hard X-ray detector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_hard_xray_detector), while [extent of the soft X-ray detector](name:extent_of_soft_xray_detector) denotes a broader detector-size quantity rather than this specifically defined X1 aperture dimension.

rows.name: electron_absorbed_wave_power
rows.source_description: Wave power absorbed by the thermal particle population
rows.documentation:
Electron absorbed wave power is the total rate of energy transfer from coherent electromagnetic waves to the electron populations. It includes direct absorption by both bulk thermal electrons and fast non-thermal electrons.

The volume-integrated electron power is defined by

$$
P_e^{\mathrm{abs}} = \int_V p_e^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV = P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{abs}} + P_{e,\mathrm{thermal}}^{\mathrm{abs}}
$$

where $P_e^{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the total electron absorbed wave power, $p_e^{\mathrm{abs}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local wave power deposition density to electrons, $V$ is the plasma volume, and the two terms are the [fast-electron absorbed wave power](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power) and [thermal-electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power). This quantity is the electron component of [absorbed wave power](name:absorbed_wave_power), excluding power absorbed directly by ions or other channels; [ion absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) represents the corresponding ion channel.

rows.name: parallel_ion_heat_convection_velocity
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Signed field-aligned convection velocity for transporting aggregate bulk-ion thermal energy in the parallel ion energy balance is the scalar coefficient multiplying bulk-ion thermal enthalpy density in the convective part of the parallel ion energy flux. It is defined along the local magnetic-field unit vector and describes the charge-state-aggregated bulk-ion population, not a single ion charge state.

The defining relation to the convective contribution to the parallel ion energy flux is

$$
q_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \frac{5}{2}\, n_i T_i\, v_{\parallel,\mathrm{heat}}^{i}
$$

where $q_{\parallel,i}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective contribution to the [parallel ion energy flux](name:parallel_ion_energy_flux), $n_i$ is the bulk-ion number density, $T_i$ is the bulk-ion temperature expressed as particle energy, and $v_{\parallel,\mathrm{heat}}^{i}$ is this velocity. The factor $5/2$ is the monatomic ideal-gas enthalpy convention.

This quantity is an effective heat-convection coefficient, not the total ion flow velocity, conductive heat flux, or total ion energy flux. As a species-level intensive quantity, it is the density-weighted mean of the corresponding charge-state-resolved ion heat-convection velocities over all ion charge states, with weights given by the charge-state number densities; the charge-state-resolved counterpart is [effective thermal ion charge-state energy velocity due to convection]. It is the parallel component of [ion heat convection velocity] and is distinct from [parallel total ion energy convection velocity](name:parallel_total_ion_energy_convection_velocity).

Sign convention: Positive when the convective contribution to the parallel ion energy flux is directed along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$.

rows.name: alfven_frequency_real_part
rows.source_description: Real part of the frequency, for a given radial position and every root found at this position
rows.documentation:
Oscillation angular frequency is the real part of the complex angular frequency of a local shear-Alfvén continuum root. It gives the signed oscillatory component of that continuum branch at a specified position across magnetic flux surfaces for one toroidal mode number.

The real part is defined from the complex continuum angular frequency by:

$$
\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\Omega_{\mathrm{A}}\right)
$$

where $\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}}$ is this oscillation angular frequency, $\Omega_{\mathrm{A}}$ is the [complex Alfvén frequency](name:alfven_frequency), and $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real-part operator.

The scope is one local shear-Alfvén continuum root at one position across the magnetic flux surfaces and one toroidal mode number; it is not an average, envelope, or sum over roots, positions, or mode numbers. The toroidal mode number $n$ is the integer Fourier index of variation in toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. This quantity excludes global eigenmode frequencies and continua not belonging to the shear-Alfvén branch.

The [complex Alfvén frequency](name:alfven_frequency) decomposes into this quantity and its imaginary companion as $\Omega_{\mathrm{A}} = \omega_{\mathrm{A,r}} + i\gamma_{\mathrm{A}}$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit and $\gamma_{\mathrm{A}}$ is the [Alfvén-frequency imaginary part](name:alfven_frequency_imaginary_part), representing growth or damping under the same complex-frequency convention. The signed value $\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}}$ identifies the selected real branch; the non-negative magnitude $|\omega_{\mathrm{A,r}}|$ is an unsigned oscillation rate and is not this quantity. The branch sign follows the phase convention that the oscillatory perturbation is proportional to $\exp[i(n\phi-\Omega_{\mathrm{A}}t)]$, where $t$ is time.

Sign convention: Positive when the temporal phase of the oscillatory factor $\exp[-i\Omega_{\mathrm{A}} t]$ decreases with increasing time, so for positive toroidal mode number $n$ the corresponding constant-phase surface moves toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with the position on the flux surface otherwise held fixed.

rows.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
rows.source_description: Collisional toroidal torque density to the fast particle population
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the local toroidal component of the angular-momentum source density deposited in co-passing fast ions by Coulomb collisions. It is the toroidal projection of the vector quantity [co-passing fast ion torque density due to collisions].

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector deposited in the co-passing fast-ion population and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

The quantity aggregates the included co-passing fast-ion population rather than resolving individual charge states; charge-state resolution is provided by [toroidal co-passing fast ion charge state torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions). Contributions from the counter-passing population are represented separately by [toroidal counter-passing fast ion torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when collisional angular-momentum transfer to co-passing fast ions is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

rows.name: accumulated_deuterium_count_due_to_gas_injection
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of deuterium atoms delivered through gas injection, expressed using an equivalent-electron weighting. It represents delivered fuel inventory rather than an instantaneous injection rate or the number of electrons currently present in the plasma.

The equivalent-electron convention is defined by

$$
N_D^{\mathrm{eq}} = Z_D N_D
$$

where $N_D^{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron inventory, $Z_D$ is the atomic number of deuterium and equals one, and $N_D$ is the cumulative number of deuterium atoms delivered after plasma breakdown.

The scope is restricted to deuterium introduced after plasma breakdown by gas injection. Contributions are accumulated over the injection history and weighted per deuterium atom; prefill delivery and other injected species are excluded. Ionization after delivery does not change the assigned equivalent-electron weighting.

The weighting convention is shared by [accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection) and [accumulated_oxygen_count_due_to_gas_injection](name:oxygen_count_accumulated_due_to_gas_injection), while this quantity remains specific to deuterium.

rows.name: vertical_coordinate_of_antenna_strap
rows.source_description: Centre height
rows.documentation:
The vertical coordinate of an antenna strap is the height coordinate of the center of its annular geometry. It identifies the strap's geometric position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity applies to the antenna strap as a whole and represents one geometric center coordinate; it is neither a plasma quantity nor a coordinate of a particular strap endpoint. No averaging, integration, or contour description is implied.

The definition follows the reference-position convention used for the [vertical coordinate of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:vertical_coordinate_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna), while retaining the antenna strap as the owning object.

rows.name: poloidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
rows.source_description: Poloidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity is the component along the poloidal basis direction of the electric current-density contribution generated by parallel viscous stress in a magnetized plasma. The projection is taken along \(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta\), the unit tangent in the direction of increasing poloidal angle \(\theta\) at fixed radial flux label \(\rho\) and toroidal angle \(\phi\) in the flux-coordinate system \((\rho,\theta,\phi)\).

The component is the projection of the parallel-viscosity current-density vector onto that poloidal tangent:

$$
J_{\Pi_\parallel,\theta}
= \hat{\mathbf{e}}_\theta \cdot \left[
J_{\Pi_\parallel,\parallel}\,\hat{\mathbf{b}}
+ \frac{\mathbf{B} \times (\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel)}{B^2}
\right]
$$

where \(J_{\Pi_\parallel,\theta}\) is the poloidal current density due to parallel viscosity, \(J_{\Pi_\parallel,\parallel}\) is the signed field-aligned projection of the same current-density contribution, \(\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/B\) is the magnetic-field unit vector, \(\mathbf{B}\) is the magnetic field, \(B=|\mathbf{B}|\), \(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel\) is the parallel viscous stress tensor, and \(\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel\) is the corresponding viscous force density. The cross-product term is the perpendicular force-balance drift contribution associated with the parallel-viscous force density.

This quantity is one directional projection of [current density due to parallel viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity). Other projections of the same contribution include [parallel current density due to parallel viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), [radial current density due to parallel viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) along \(\hat{R}\), [toroidal current density due to parallel viscosity](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) along \(\hat{\phi}\), and [vertical current density due to parallel viscosity](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) along \(+\hat{Z}\) in the right-handed cylindrical \((R,\phi,Z)\) frame, where \(R\) is major radius, \(\phi\) is toroidal angle, and \(Z\) is vertical height. It is distinct from [poloidal current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), which uses the perpendicular-viscous stress contribution rather than \(\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel\).

Sign convention: Positive when the current-density contribution points in the direction of increasing poloidal angle \(\theta\) in the flux-coordinate system \((\rho,\theta,\phi)\).

rows.name: toroidal_co_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force
rows.source_description: Toroidal torque due to radial currents
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged toroidal angular-momentum source density delivered to co-passing particles by the Lorentz force. It is the toroidal projection of the [co-passing torque density due to the J cross B force].

The defining relation is

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{co}}^{J\times B}(\psi)=\left\langle R\left[(J_{\mathrm{co},n}\hat{n}_{\psi})\times\mathbf{B}\right]\cdot\hat{\phi}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $\psi$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $J_{\mathrm{co},n}\hat{n}_{\psi}$ is the co-passing current density normal to that surface, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $R$ is major radius, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The brackets denote an average over the complete flux surface.

The co-passing population consists of passing particle orbits moving in the co-current direction; counter-passing and trapped contributions are excluded and are represented by the [toroidal counter-passing torque density due to the J cross B force](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and [toroidal trapped torque density due to the J cross B force](name:toroidal_trapped_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force).

Sign convention: Positive when the Lorentz-force torque on the co-passing population acts in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ about the symmetry axis.

rows.name: per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_charge_state_power
rows.source_description: Wave power absorbed by the fast particle population per toroidal mode number
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the coherent-electromagnetic-wave power absorbed directly by fast ions in one specified charge state, resolved by toroidal Fourier mode and integrated over the plasma volume. It is a modal component of [fast-ion charge-state power](name:fast_ion_charge_state_absorbed_wave_power), excluding collisional energy exchange between plasma populations.

The volume-integrated modal power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast},q}(n_\phi)=\int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}}p_{\mathrm{abs,fast},q}(n_\phi,\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $n_\phi$ is the toroidal Fourier mode number, $q$ is the ion charge state, $p_{\mathrm{abs,fast},q}$ is the corresponding local absorbed-power density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume.

Unlike [per-toroidal-mode fast-ion power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_power_density), this quantity is volume-integrated and retains ion charge-state resolution; it is distinct from the corresponding thermal-ion modal power [per-toroidal-mode thermal-ion charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power).

rows.name: ion_charge_state_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Ion charge-state energy flux at the wall due to recombination quantifies the rate at which recombination-associated energy from incident plasma ions of a specified species and charge state leaves a plasma-facing surface per unit area. It is the ion-associated component for that incident-ion population, not the incident plasma energy flux or heat deposited in the wall material.

The ion charge-state recombination energy flux at wall location $\mathbf{x}_w$ for incident species $i$ and charge state $\zeta$ is defined as the product-energy moment of the outgoing ion-associated recombination source:

$$
Q^{\mathrm{ion}}_{\mathrm{rec},i,\zeta}(\mathbf{x}_w) = \sum_{c,\,a,\,k}\int E_\mathrm{out}\,\frac{d\Gamma^{\mathrm{ion}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}}{dE_\mathrm{out}}(\mathbf{x}_w,E_\mathrm{out})\,dE_\mathrm{out}
$$

where $i$ identifies the incident-ion species, $\zeta$ the incident-ion charge state, $c$ an ion-associated surface recombination or neutralization channel, $a$ the emitted product species, $k$ the product internal state or emission class, $E_\mathrm{out}$ the energy carried into the plasma-facing half-space by an emitted product or quantum, and $d\Gamma^{\mathrm{ion}}_{i,\zeta,c,a,k}/dE_\mathrm{out}$ the corresponding outgoing recombination-product flux distribution with respect to product energy. For discrete product energies, the integral is replaced by the corresponding sum.

This quantity resolves the incident-ion species and charge state within the ion-associated recombination energy channel. Summing over incident-ion charge states and incident-ion species gives [ion energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:ion_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination); the broader [energy flux at the wall due to recombination](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination) also includes recombination energy channels outside this ion-associated component. It is the energy-weighted counterpart of [particle flux at the wall due to recombination] for the same surface recombination source.

rows.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_gyrocenter_current_density_bessel_1
rows.source_description: Normalised parallel current density
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the first-order Bessel-weighted, field-parallel current-density moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution. It represents the electromagnetic response of a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode in the gyrocenter description.

The normalized moment is defined by

$$
j_{parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{q}{j_{\mathrm{ref}}} \int v_{\parallel} J_1(k_{\perp}\rho)\,\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $j_{\parallel,J_1}^{\mathrm{norm}}$ is the normalized Bessel-weighted parallel current-density moment, $q$ is the charge of the represented particle species, $j_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference current-density scale, $v_{\parallel}$ is the velocity component along the local equilibrium magnetic field, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel function of the first kind, $k_{\perp}$ is the perpendicular wave-number magnitude, $\rho$ is the particle gyroradius, $\delta f_{\mathrm{gc}}(\mathbf{v})$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space coordinate, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity is restricted to the perturbed gyrocenter distribution, the field-parallel velocity channel, and the first-order Bessel weighting. Its aggregation convention is the charge-weighted moment shown in the integral; it is not an unweighted density moment, a perpendicular current channel, an equilibrium contribution, or a particle-frame moment.
