It is the normalized, parallel specialization of the vector [normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density), with the additional $J_1$ finite-Larmor-radius weighting. Removing that weighting gives the corresponding [parallel normalized gyrocenter perturbed current density](name:parallel_normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_current_density).

Sign convention: Positive when the charge-weighted perturbed current is directed along the local equilibrium magnetic field, whose orientation is expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: trapped_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
rows.source_description: Collisional power density to the fast particle population
rows.documentation:
Trapped fast-ion power density due to collisions is the local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to fast ions on trapped guiding-center orbits per unit volume. A trapped orbit mirror-reflects between magnetic turning points rather than completing a full poloidal transit. This is the trapped-orbit component of [fast-ion power density due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), distinct from the [counter-passing fast-ion power density due to collisions](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions).

For a fast-ion species, the orbit-restricted collisional power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{trapped,coll}}(\mathbf{x},t) = \int \chi_{\mathrm{trapped}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,\frac{1}{2}m_i v^2\,C_{\mathrm{coll}}[f_{\mathrm{fast}}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position in m, $t$ is time in s, $m_i$ is fast-ion mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity in m s$^{-1}$, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$, $f_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion distribution function, $C_{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the Coulomb collision operator, $\chi_{\mathrm{trapped}}$ is a dimensionless indicator selecting trapped guiding-center orbits, and $d^3v$ is velocity-space volume. The integral is algebraic: positive values denote net collisional energy gain by trapped fast ions, while negative values denote net collisional energy loss. Contributions from co-passing and counter-passing orbits are excluded.

rows.name: line_averaged_helium_4_density
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
The line-averaged helium-4 ion number density is the path average of the local helium-4 ion density along a specified chord through the plasma. It represents an effective density for that chord, not the local value at a point or a volume-wide mean.

The line average is defined by

$$
\overline{n}_{{}^4\mathrm{He}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{0}^{L} n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(l)\,dl
$$

where $n_{{}^4\mathrm{He}}(l)$ is the local helium-4 ion number density from [helium_4_density](name:helium_4_density), $l$ is distance along the chord, and $L$ is the chord length; $l$ and $L$ are measured in m.

The average includes the local helium-4 ion density along the specified path and uses uniform path-length weighting. Unlike [volume_averaged_helium_4_density](name:volume_averaged_helium_4_density), it is not averaged over the confined plasma volume.

rows.name: helium_4_density_at_pedestal_top
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
Helium-4 ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local concentration of helium-4 ions at the inner shoulder of the H-mode transport barrier.

The charge-state-summed density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{He4}} = \sum_{q=1}^{2} n_{\mathrm{He4}}^{(q)}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{He4}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{He4}}^{(q)}$ is the local number density of helium-4 ions in charge state $q$, and $q$ is the positive ion charge-state index. The sum includes singly and doubly ionized helium-4 and excludes neutral helium-4.

This quantity applies specifically to the helium-4 isotope and is evaluated locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate at the pedestal top](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is not a flux-surface average, line-of-sight average, or total ion density.

It is the helium-4 species specialization of [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top). It differs from [helium-4 density at the plasma boundary](name:helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary) because the latter is evaluated at the plasma-boundary locus, and it is the mass-isotope counterpart of [helium-3 density at the pedestal top](name:helium_3_density_at_pedestal_top).

rows.name: tilt_angle_of_passive_loop
rows.source_description: Inclination of second angle TBD
rows.documentation:
The tilt angle specifies the orientation of a passive conducting loop element’s directed geometric reference axis in the poloidal plane. It describes the overall orientation of the element, not an inclination parameter defining the shape of an oblique cross-section, and is analogous to the orientation defined for a [tilt angle of a plasma filament](name:tilt_angle_of_plasma_filament).

Let the reference-axis direction have components $t_R$ and $t_Z$ along the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. The tilt angle is defined by

$$
\theta_{\mathrm{tilt}} = \operatorname{atan2}(t_Z,t_R)
$$

where $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the directed angle from the outward $+R$ direction toward the upward $+Z$ direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the reference axis rotates from $+R$ toward $+Z$.

rows.name: vertical_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field
rows.source_description: Z component of the vacuum error magnetic field
rows.documentation:
Vertical non-axisymmetric magnetic field is the vertical component of the toroidally varying part of the external-coil vacuum magnetic field in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It is the signed Z-directed projection of the [non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), not the total magnetic field.

At fixed major radius and vertical height, its defining toroidal-mean subtraction is

$$
B_{\mathrm{na},Z}(R,\phi,Z)=B_{\mathrm{vac},Z}(R,\phi,Z)-\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi}B_{\mathrm{vac},Z}(R,\phi',Z)\,d\phi'
$$

where $B_{\mathrm{na},Z}$ is the vertical non-axisymmetric component, $B_{\mathrm{vac},Z}$ is the vertical vacuum-field component, $R$ and $Z$ are major-radius and vertical coordinates measured in meters, and $\phi$ and $\phi'$ are toroidal angles measured in radians.

The quantity excludes the toroidally averaged vacuum field and any plasma-response field. It is distinct from the [radial non-axisymmetric magnetic field](name:radial_non_axisymmetric_magnetic_field), which is the corresponding radial projection.

Sign convention: Positive when $B_{\mathrm{na},Z}$ points in the $+Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis.

rows.name: external_loop_voltage
rows.source_description: External voltage, i.e. time derivative of psi_external_average (with a minus sign : - d_psi_external_average/d_time)
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the inductive electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage produced by time-varying poloidal magnetic flux generated by active coil circuits and magnetically coupled passive conducting structures. It excludes resistive voltage drops and other non-inductive contributions.

The contribution is defined by Faraday's law:

$$
V_{\mathrm{ext}}(t) = -\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the externally generated poloidal magnetic flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit and $t$ is time. It contributes to the total [loop voltage at the plasma boundary](name:loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary); currents in passive conductors are represented by the linked-flux response of structures such as those described by [current of passive structure](name:current_of_passive_structure).

Sign convention: Positive when the induced electromotive force has a positive line integral in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
rows.source_description: Imaginary part
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the imaginary quadrature of the radial component of a first-order perturbed magnetic vector potential eigenfunction in the confined plasma.

The complex radial component is decomposed as

$$
\widetilde{A}_r = A_{r,\mathrm{R}} + i A_{r,\mathrm{I}}
$$

where $\widetilde{A}_r$ is the complex radial component of the perturbed magnetic vector potential, $A_{r,\mathrm{R}}$ is its real part, $A_{r,\mathrm{I}}$ is its imaginary part, and $i$ is the imaginary unit. This quantity is $A_{r,\mathrm{I}}$.

The definition is restricted to the radial component in the confined plasma and to the selected linear MHD eigenfunction; it is not a sum over vector components or modes. It excludes the real quadrature and the poloidal and toroidal components. Together with the real part, it fully specifies the complex component and is the imaginary-part specialization of the [radial perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential).

rows.name: parallel_fast_neutral_pressure
rows.source_description: Fast (non-thermal) parallel pressure  (sum over charge states when multiple charge states are considered)
rows.documentation:
Parallel fast neutral pressure is the scalar field-aligned component of the kinetic pressure tensor of suprathermal neutral particles. It represents the random kinetic stress associated with neutral motion parallel to the local magnetic field, summed over all internal quantum states.

$$
P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fn}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf P_{\mathrm{fn}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $P_{\parallel,\mathrm{fn}}$ is the parallel fast neutral pressure, $\mathbf P_{\mathrm{fn}}$ is the fast-neutral kinetic pressure tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

This quantity is the field-aligned component of [fast neutral pressure](name:fast_neutral_pressure) and, together with [perpendicular fast neutral pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure), defines its gyrotropic decomposition. The state-resolved counterpart [parallel fast neutral internal-state pressure](name:parallel_fast_neutral_internal_state_pressure) separates contributions by internal neutral state.

rows.name: maximum_of_back_surface_neutron_flux
rows.source_description: Maximum neutron flux escaping from the back of the blanket module
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the greatest local neutron energy flux crossing outward through the rear surface of one breeding blanket module. It measures the escaping neutron load relevant to attenuation toward vessel structures.

The maximum is defined from the local back-surface neutron energy flux as

$$
q_{n,\max} = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S_{\mathrm{back}}} q_n(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $q_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neutron energy flux at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $S_{\mathrm{back}}$ is the rear surface of the module.

The quantity applies to fusion neutrons from all included neutron energies, fusion reaction channels, and reacting populations, aggregated into a single local energy-flux value before taking the maximum over the rear surface of one module. It represents neutrons escaping outward from the module and excludes a surface-integrated module power and neutron flux incident on the module's front surface.

It is the maximum-over-surface transformation of [back-surface neutron flux](name:back_surface_neutron_flux), which describes the local value without selecting its maximum. It is distinct from [incident neutron power of a breeder blanket module](name:incident_neutron_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which is the total neutron power arriving at the module, and from [nuclear heating power of a breeder blanket module](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_module), which describes energy deposited by neutron interactions within the module.

rows.name: plasma_energy
rows.documentation:
Plasma energy is the volume-integrated internal kinetic energy carried by all confined electron and ion populations, including thermal and suprathermal populations. It is the all-population stored particle energy of the confined plasma, not a thermal-only component.

A pressure-tensor definition gives the stored particle energy without assuming isotropic distributions:

$$
W_\mathrm{p} = \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_a \frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_a\, dV
$$

where $W_\mathrm{p}$ is the plasma energy, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $a$ labels the electron, ion, and modeled suprathermal populations included in the confined plasma, $\mathbf{P}_a$ is the pressure tensor of population $a$ in its local mean-flow frame, and $dV$ is the scalar volume element. For isotropic populations this reduces to the pressure-sum relation with energy density $3p_\mathrm{tot}/2$, where $p_\mathrm{tot}=\sum_a p_a$; for a gyrotropic anisotropic population the contribution is $p_{\perp a}+p_{\parallel a}/2$.

This quantity excludes electromagnetic-field energy, electrostatic-field energy, rest-mass energy, and organized macroscopic bulk-flow energy. [Electron energy](name:electron_energy), [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), and [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy) are component contributions, while [total plasma energy] and [total particle energy] denote the corresponding all-population stored particle-energy concept when the naming emphasizes totality.

rows.name: current_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
The quantity is the net toroidal electric current carried by the plasma as a result of non-inductive current-drive mechanisms. It excludes current produced by the transformer-induced electric field and includes the algebraic sum of the included non-inductive contributions. The plasma-specific realization is [plasma current due to non-inductive current drive](name:current_due_to_non_inductive_current_drive).

The current is defined by the flux of non-inductive current density through a poloidal cross-section:

$$
I_{\mathrm{NI}} = \int_{S_p} \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{NI}} \cdot d\mathbf{S}
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{NI}}$ is the non-inductive current, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{NI}}$ is the corresponding electric-current density, and $d\mathbf{S}$ is the oriented area element of the poloidal cross-section. Contributions such as [current due to electron-cyclotron current drive](name:current_due_to_electron_cyclotron_current_drive) and [current due to ion-cyclotron current drive](name:current_due_to_ion_cyclotron_current_drive) are instances of this quantity, whereas [plasma current due to ohmic induction] is excluded.

Sign convention: Positive when the net current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: maximum_angle_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
rows.source_description: Maximum angular displacement with respect to the reference position, counter-clockwise around the direction vector
rows.documentation:
The upper mechanical travel limit is the greatest permitted value of the mirror’s signed rotation angle, bounding the accessible steering range of the launcher. It is a limit of the mechanical actuator, not the mirror angle during a particular operating condition.

Let $\theta$ denote the signed mirror angle defined by [angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror]. The upper limit $\theta_{\max}$ is defined by

$$
\theta_{\max} = \sup\{\theta \mid \theta\text{ is mechanically accessible}\}
$$

The quantity excludes the lower travel limit and does not describe the mirror’s position unless that position equals the upper boundary of the allowed range.

Sign convention: Positive when the mirror rotates in the positive sense defined for [angle of electron-cyclotron launcher mirror].

rows.name: flux_surface_averaged_time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude
rows.source_description: Normalised perturbed parallel magnetic field
rows.documentation:
This quantity represents the normalized amplitude of the magnetic-field perturbation parallel to the local equilibrium magnetic field, characterizing electromagnetic compressional fluctuations after time and flux-surface averaging. The magnitude removes the sign and phase of the parallel perturbation.

For each retained wavevector component $k_y$, the quantity is defined by

$$
Q(k_y)=\left\langle\left\langle\sum_{k_x}\frac{\left|\delta\mathbf{B}(k_x,k_y,t)\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}_0\right|}{B_{\mathrm{ref}}}\right\rangle_t\right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $Q(k_y)$ is the normalized fluctuation amplitude, $k_x$ and $k_y$ are wavevector components, $t$ is time, $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed magnetic-field component, $\hat{\mathbf b}_0$ is the unit vector along the local equilibrium magnetic field, $B_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference magnetic-field magnitude, and the angle brackets denote time and flux-surface averages.

The quantity applies to the parallel magnetic perturbation only; it excludes perpendicular perturbations and the unperturbed equilibrium field. Its aggregation convention is summation over $k_x$, followed by time averaging and flux-surface averaging, while dependence on $k_y$ is retained.

Relative to the [time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude](name:time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude), this quantity adds flux-surface averaging while preserving the same perturbation, parallel projection, normalization, magnitude, and time-averaging operations.

rows.name: normalized_particle_mass
rows.source_description: Normalised mass
rows.documentation:
This quantity expresses the inertial mass of one particle of a specified species relative to a strictly positive reference mass. It is the normalized counterpart of [particle mass], rather than an independent mass or mass density.

The normalized particle mass is defined by

$$
\bar{m}_s = \frac{m_s}{m_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$ and $m_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference mass used by the normalization. The result preserves the relative inertial ordering of species while removing the mass scale from normalized equations of motion.

The reference mass must be kept fixed when comparing normalized masses; changing it rescales all such ratios by the same factor. This quantity excludes mass associated with a population or volume and does not represent a mass density.

rows.name: deposited_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_halo_current
rows.source_description: Power deposited on this divertor target due to electric currents (positive means power is deposited on the target)
rows.documentation:
Deposited power at a divertor target due to halo current is the electrical work rate delivered to one divertor target by halo current crossing the plasma-facing target surface. Halo current is current in the edge or scrape-off-layer plasma that closes through conducting plasma-facing structures; this quantity selects only its contribution to current-driven target loading.

For a target surface with defined local current density and potential drop, the target-surface definition is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{halo},t} = \int_{A_t} j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}(\mathbf{r})\,\Delta\Phi_t(\mathbf{r})\,dA
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{halo},t}$ is this deposited power, $A_t$ is the portion of the plasma-facing target surface intercepted by halo current, $dA$ is a target-surface area element, $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ is the conventional halo-current density projected on the local unit normal directed from the plasma into the target material, and $\Delta\Phi_t = \Phi_{\mathrm{plasma}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the local plasma-to-target potential drop.

The surface integral of $j_{\mathrm{halo},n}^{\mathrm{in}}$ over $A_t$ is the halo-current contribution to [current at divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target). This quantity excludes the conductive, convective, radiative, and neutral-particle target-power channels, and excludes current-driven target power not produced by halo current; together with other current-driven components it is part of [power at divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target), while sums over divertor targets contribute to [power of divertor]. It is zero when no halo-current electrical work is deposited on the target; positive values denote net energy deposition on that target.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional halo current crosses from the plasma into the target along the plasma-to-material surface normal across a positive plasma-to-target potential drop.

rows.name: surface_current_per_toroidal_and_poloidal_mode_number_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
rows.source_description: Spectrum of the total surface current on the antenna strap and passive components expressed in poloidal and toroidal modes
rows.documentation:
The quantity is the Fourier-mode coefficient of the total surface current associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna. It combines the current contributions from the antenna straps and passive components before resolving their poloidal and toroidal variation.

For the Fourier convention used here, the coefficient for poloidal mode number $m$ and toroidal mode number $n$ is

$$
\widetilde{I}_{mn}=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^2}\int_{0}^{2\pi}\int_{0}^{2\pi} I_s(\theta,\phi)e^{-i(m\theta+n\phi)}\,d\theta\,d\phi
$$

where $\widetilde{I}_{mn}$ is the modal surface-current coefficient, $I_s(\theta,\phi)$ is the signed total surface-current distribution, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $Z$ is vertical height, $m$ and $n$ are integer poloidal and toroidal mode numbers, respectively, $i$ is the imaginary unit, and $\pi$ is the circle constant.

The quantity is aggregated over all straps and passive components belonging to the antenna, while each pair $(m,n)$ identifies one Fourier component rather than a sum over mode numbers. It is therefore distinct from [wave current of an antenna strap], which describes current confined to an individual strap, and from [wave current of an antenna strap amplitude], which describes the peak magnitude of that strap current. The coefficient's sign and phase follow the chosen positive surface-current direction, angular origins, and Fourier convention shown above.

rows.name: toroidal_conductivity
rows.source_description: Toroidal component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Toroidal conductivity is the toroidal-toroidal projection of the local electrical-conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, whose basis is $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$. It is the directional coefficient within the parent [plasma electrical conductivity](name:plasma_electrical_conductivity) response.

The local conductive response is defined by

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}}=\boldsymbol{\sigma}\cdot\mathbf{E},\qquad J_{\mathrm{cond},\phi}=\sum_{j\in\{R,\phi,Z\}}\sigma_{\phi j}E_j,\qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{toroidal}}=\sigma_{\phi\phi}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive current-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is the local electrical-conductivity tensor, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $J_{\mathrm{cond},\phi}$ is its toroidal component, $\sigma_{\phi j}$ couples the electric-field component in direction $j$ to the toroidal current component, and $E_j$ is the electric-field component in direction $j$; $j$ ranges over the cylindrical directions $R$, $\phi$, and $Z$.

This quantity denotes only the same-direction toroidal coefficient $\sigma_{\phi\phi}$ and is not the total toroidal current density or a sum of all tensor contributions. Off-diagonal terms may also contribute to the toroidal conductive current, but they are excluded from this coefficient. Unlike [radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity) and [toroidal electric field](name:toroidal_electric_field), it is a material-response coefficient rather than a field component; it is the toroidal member of the conductivity tensor family.

rows.name: neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall
rows.source_description: One scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Incident neutral particle flux at a plasma-facing wall quantifies the arrival rate of neutral atoms or molecules in one specified electronic, vibrational, or rotational internal state per unit wall area. It is an incoming surface flux, not an emitted or net flux.

$$
\Gamma_{n,s} = \frac{dN_{n,s}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $\Gamma_{n,s}$ is the state-resolved neutral particle flux, $N_{n,s}$ is the number of arriving neutral particles in internal state $s$, $A$ is wall-surface area, and $t$ is time.

Unlike the state-summed [neutral particle flux at the wall], this quantity resolves the internal-state contribution. It has no process attribution; the recombination-specific subset is [incident neutral internal-state particle flux at the wall due to recombination](name:incident_neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

rows.name: accumulated_deuterated_methane_prefill_count
rows.source_description: Value
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative amount of deuterated methane introduced during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron inventory. It represents neutral CD4 molecules before plasma breakdown, not the post-breakdown gas-injection inventory.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm prefill} = \int_{t_0}^{t_b} \dot{N}_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm CD_4}(t)\,dt = 10N_{\rm CD_4}^{\rm prefill}
$$

where $N_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm prefill}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron inventory, $\dot{N}_{e,\rm eq}^{\rm CD_4}$ is the [deuterated methane source rate](name:deuterated_methane_source_rate), $t_0$ and $t_b$ delimit prefill before breakdown, and $N_{\rm CD_4}^{\rm prefill}$ is the accumulated number of CD4 molecules. The factor ten is the total electron count of one fully ionizable CD4 molecule. The species-resolved quantity contributes to the [accumulated total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count), which sums equivalent-electron inventories across gas species.

rows.name: vertical_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia
rows.source_description: Component along the height axis, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Vertical projection of the current density due to ion inertia is the electric-current component generated by inertial acceleration terms in the ion-fluid momentum equation. It includes the $Z$ component of the polarization-type current associated with finite ion mass and time-dependent or convective ion-fluid acceleration, taken along $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The vertical component is the projection of the ion-inertia current density vector onto $\hat{Z}$:

$$
J_{Z,\mathrm{inertia}} = \hat{Z}\cdot \left(\frac{m_i n_i}{B^2}\mathbf{B}\times \frac{d_i\mathbf{v}_i}{dt}\right)
$$

where $J_{Z,\mathrm{inertia}}$ is the vertical projection, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, $\mathbf{v}_i$ is the ion-fluid velocity, and $d_i/dt=\partial/\partial t+\mathbf{v}_i\cdot\nabla$ is the ion convective derivative.

This quantity is the $Z$ projection of [current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), not the full vector, its magnitude, or its divergence. The matched right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ components are [radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:radial_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), [toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia), and this vertical projection; the field-aligned projection is [parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_ion_inertia). It excludes turbulent or anomalous-transport contributions such as [vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_anomalous_transport).

Sign convention: Positive when the ion-inertia current density points in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

rows.name: vertical_total_current_density
rows.source_description: Component along the height axis, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
Vertical total current density is the component of the aggregated current-density vector [total current density] resolved along the vertical direction. It combines ohmic, bootstrap, and externally driven contributions over all included plasma species and charge states, distinguishing it from the generic [vertical current density].

The defining projection is:

$$
J_{\mathrm{v,total}} = \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{total}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $J_{\mathrm{v,total}}$ is the vertical total current density, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{total}}$ is the aggregated conventional current-density vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional current has a component in the $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ direction, corresponding to increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

rows.name: electron_density_at_pellet_path
rows.source_description: Electron density along the pellet path
rows.documentation:
The quantity is the local number density of free electrons in the background plasma at each point traversed by an injected pellet. It describes the plasma encountered by the pellet, not electron content in pellet material or electron production by ablation.

At a path point, the electron number density is defined by the local number-to-volume ratio:

$$
n_e = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{\Delta N_e}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_e$ is the electron number density, $\Delta N_e$ is the number of free electrons in the volume element $\Delta V$, and $\Delta V$ is the volume element centered at the path point.

The quantity is evaluated locally along the pellet trajectory and is distinct from the [electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection](name:electron_source_rate_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection), which describes electron production rather than background density. It has the same physical meaning as [electron density at the launching position](name:electron_density_at_launching_position), but at a different locus.

rows.name: current_at_divertor_target
rows.source_description: Total current incident on this target
rows.documentation:
Net conventional electric current delivered by the plasma to one divertor target surface is the signed charge-flow rate crossing the plasma-facing target interface, integrated over the wetted strike zone. It represents the net incident conventional current carried by charged plasma particles to that target.

The target current is defined by the surface integral of incident conventional-current density over the wetted target region:

$$
I_{\mathrm{target}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{wet}}} \mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{target}} \, dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the current at the divertor target, $S_{\mathrm{wet}}$ is the wetted strike-zone part of the target surface, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident conventional electric-current density due to plasma particles at the target surface, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_{\mathrm{target}}$ is the unit normal directed from the plasma into the target material, and $dA$ is the surface area element. For multiple charged species, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the charge-weighted sum of their incident particle flux densities, so ion and electron contributions enter with opposite electric-charge signs.

The scope is one physical divertor target surface; the aggregation convention is the surface integral over the wetted strike-zone region of that target. It excludes neighboring targets, non-target plasma-facing components, and return currents in external conducting structures. It is a net conventional current, not an ion-only current, an electron-only current, an unsigned collected-current magnitude, or a particle flux.

Summing this quantity over the target surfaces belonging to a divertor gives the target-current contribution to [current of divertor](name:current_of_divertor). If a target is partitioned into tiles, summing [current of divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile) over the tiles that cover the same wetted target region gives this per-target quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional current carried by charged plasma particles is directed from the plasma into the divertor target material.

rows.name: implicit_ion_energy_source_rate
rows.source_description: Implicit part of the source term, i.e. to be multiplied by the equation's primary quantity
rows.documentation:
This quantity is the stiff implicit linear coefficient of the energy source or sink for the applicable ion population. It represents the temperature-dependent part of the ion energy source that is treated implicitly during time integration.

The implicit ion energy-source contribution is defined by

$$
S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} = \alpha_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} T_i
$$

where $S_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit ion energy source contribution, $\alpha_{E,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is this source-rate coefficient, $T_i$ is the local ion temperature, and the superscript $\mathrm{imp}$ denotes the implicit contribution. The subscript $E$ identifies the energy channel and $i$ identifies the applicable ion population.

The coefficient applies to the ion-species member represented by the ion channel; it is not summed over all ion species, does not represent a total-ion quantity, and does not select a particular ion charge state. It belongs to the energy channel and is distinct from particle- and momentum-source coefficients. The explicit, non-stiff remainder of the ion energy source is excluded. For positive ion temperature, a positive coefficient produces an energy gain and a negative coefficient produces an energy loss.

Its role is analogous to the electron-channel coefficient [implicit electron energy-source rate coefficient](name:implicit_electron_energy_source_rate), while [total implicit ion particle-source rate coefficient](name:total_implicit_ion_particle_source_rate) differs in both transport channel and ion aggregation.

rows.name: width_of_iron_core_segment
rows.source_description: Horizontal full width
rows.documentation:
The iron core segment width is the complete radial span between the inner and outer faces of its rectangular cross-section. It is a geometric extent, not the radial position of the segment or the curvature radius of an arc boundary.

The width is defined by

$$
w_{\rm iron} = R_{\rm outer} - R_{\rm inner}
$$

where $R_{\rm outer}$ and $R_{\rm inner}$ are the major-radius coordinates in meters of the outer and inner radial faces, respectively, and $w_{\rm iron}$ is the resulting full extent. The width complements the [height of the iron core segment](name:height_of_iron_core_segment), while the [outer radius of the iron core segment](name:outer_radius_of_iron_core_segment) identifies a boundary position rather than a cross-sectional span.

rows.name: radial_electric_field
rows.source_description: Radial component, one scalar value is provided per element in the grid subset.
rows.documentation:
The radial electric field is the component of the [electric field](name:electric_field) vector that gives the force per unit positive stationary test charge along the direction of increasing major radius. It includes electrostatic, inductive, and electromagnetic-wave contributions, like the [vertical electric field](name:vertical_electric_field).

The radial component is defined by

$$
E_R = \mathbf{E} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}
$$

where $E_R$ is the radial electric-field component, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. The projection uses the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is increasing toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Radial means the cylindrical $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ direction and is not synonymous with the normal to a magnetic flux surface.

Sign convention: Positive when $E_R$ points toward increasing major radius $R$.
